summaries.summary: Salesforce Hosted MCP Servers are Salesforce-run MCP endpoints, GA since 2026-04-29 for Enterprise Edition and above plus Developer Edition, and intended for orgs with Flex Credits. Admins activate them in Setup > API Catalog > MCP Servers; auth needs an External Client App with mcp_api and refresh_token scopes, not a Connected App or the api scope. Tool calls run as the signed-in user. Standard servers include sobject-reads, sobject-mutations, sobject-deletes, sobject-all and data360; some details rest on secondary sources.

The Salesforce Integration user license, introduced in Winter '23, grants API-only access through the Minimum Access - API Only Integrations profile. Extra rights come from permission sets on the Salesforce API Integration permission set license. It is the recommended identity for external agents, set as the execution user of a client credentials app. Enterprise, Unlimited and Performance orgs get five free licenses and Developer Edition gets one.

Max Edition is the top Salesforce edition, launched 2026-09-03 alongside Core and Advanced, and it replaced Agentforce 1 Edition. It costs $550/user/month including the Agentforce add-on and includes 2.75 million Flex Credits per org per year, the main budget for agent usage. Existing Agentforce 1 customers can upgrade at no extra cost. Earlier credit figures (1M, 2.5M) conflict, so the credit history is unconfirmed.

The Salesforce Models API serves LLMs at the api.salesforce.com ai/gpt/v1 base URL using fully qualified sfdc_ai__ model aliases. Access needs an OrgJWT minted by a connected app with the sfap_api scope via the client_credentials flow; an unsigned sf org display session token returns 404. Its GA status and full endpoint list are unconfirmed.

Salesforce MFA has been contractually required since 2022-02-01 and is enforced for all users from 2026-06-26, after which the direct UI login MFA setting cannot be turned off. SSO logins count only if the IdP sends valid AMR/ACR claims. Admins and users with powerful permissions such as Modify All Data need phishing-resistant MFA. Supported methods are Salesforce Authenticator, TOTP apps, security keys and built-in authenticators.

The Salesforce OAuth 2.0 client credentials flow is the recommended machine-to-machine auth for external agents, replacing the retiring username-password flow. Tokens are issued for a configured execution user (needing API Only, typically an Integration user) at the My Domain oauth2/token endpoint; scopes are set on the app and no refresh token is returned. Anyone holding the consumer key and secret can mint tokens. Agent API and the Models API both use it.

The Salesforce REST API is the core org data API at the My Domain services/data/vXX.X base URL with OAuth Bearer tokens; the current version is v68.0 (Winter '27). For agents, Salesforce recommends an Integration user with permission sets plus an External Client App using client credentials. Calls time out after 10 minutes, composite requests allow 25 subrequests and graphs 500 nodes, and usage shows in the Sforce-Limit-Info header and the limits endpoint.

Salesforce Shield is a Salesforce security add-on bundling Event Monitoring (80+ event types including agent actions, streaming to SIEM), Platform Encryption (BYOK and externally held keys, covering Data 360), Field Audit Trail (up to 200 fields per object for up to 10 years) and Data Detect. It matters for auditing and protecting agent activity. Components can be bought separately and pricing is quote-based.

SAML 2.0 is the open federation standard used for human single sign-on across the platforms covered. Claude, AWS IAM Identity Center, Databricks, Google Cloud Identity, Oracle identity domains and Cloud EPM, ChatGPT Business and above, and Snowflake (TYPE = SAML2, native Okta and Entra ID support) all support it. Salesforce SAML support via My Domain is noted but unverified. It covers people signing in, not agent or service authentication.

SCIM is the open standard for provisioning users and groups from an identity provider, used by AWS IAM Identity Center, Databricks (as a fallback to automatic identity management, and unable to sync service principals), OpenAI API Platform, ChatGPT Enterprise and Edu (including service accounts), Oracle Cloud EPM, Snowflake and Gemini Enterprise. Google announced SCIM for Workforce Identity Federation at Next '26, and Gemini Enterprise Okta SCIM autocomplete has been GA since 2026-08-20.

SECURITYADMIN is a Snowflake system role that holds MANAGE GRANTS and inherits USERADMIN. It matters for agent setups because it grants the tool, warehouse, database and schema privileges for agent runtime roles, applies authentication policies and creates network policies. Snowflake OAuth and External OAuth block it by default.

Select AI is an Oracle Autonomous AI Database feature that turns natural language into SQL, with actions runsql, showsql, explainsql, narrate and chat. It uses AI profiles created with DBMS_CLOUD_AI.CREATE_PROFILE and set per session. Providers include OCI Generative AI, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Cohere, Google, Anthropic, Hugging Face, Amazon Bedrock (aws) and OpenAI-compatible endpoints.

Select AI Agent is Oracle's in-database agent framework in Autonomous AI Database, in package DBMS_CLOUD_AI_AGENT, for building agents, tools, tasks and teams run with RUN_TEAM or SELECT AI agent. Built-in tools are SQL, RAG, WEBSEARCH and NOTIFICATION plus custom PL/SQL, and teams run sequentially or under a supervisor. Its tools back the Autonomous AI Database MCP Server, and it reached Dedicated Exadata on 2026-02-03.

Semantic Kernel is Microsoft's earlier agent and AI orchestration SDK, now succeeded by Microsoft Agent Framework (1.0 on 2026-04-03), built by the same teams with a published migration guide. Foundry's Semantic Kernel-based agent framework is now the Agent Framework SDK. Microsoft has stated no end-of-life date; secondary sources call it maintenance mode, which is unconfirmed officially.

Service account impersonation is a Google Cloud mechanism that lets a principal obtain short-lived tokens for a service account instead of using keys, with audit logs recording both caller and service account. It needs roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator on the target and the IAM Credentials API enabled. In gcloud it is set per command with --impersonate-service-account, CLI-wide via config, or for ADC via application-default login.

Service Account Token Creator (roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator) is the Google Cloud IAM role containing iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken, required for service account impersonation. Agent builders need it for impersonated Gemini Enterprise API calls, and the Agent Platform Service Agent needs it in the project of a cross-project Agent Runtime service account.

Service Account User (roles/iam.serviceAccountUser, permission iam.serviceAccounts.actAs) is the Google Cloud IAM role needed to attach a service account to a resource. Agent builders need it on the runtime service account for day-one Agent Platform access, for deploying to Agent Runtime with a custom service account, and for deploying to Cloud Run.

The Slack MCP server is Slack's hosted MCP endpoint at mcp.slack.com/mcp using Streamable HTTP and JSON-RPC 2.0. It supports neither SSE nor Dynamic Client Registration and requires confidential OAuth from a registered directory-published or internal app. Tools cover search, messages, canvases, users, files and lists, rate-limited at Web API tiers (Tier 2 to Tier 4), and app IP allowlists apply.

Snowflake is a cloud data platform running on AWS, Azure and Google Cloud, with accounts grouped into organizations and AI features under Cortex AI. For agent builders it offers typed users (PERSON, SERVICE, SERVICE_AGENT), SAML and OIDC SSO, a managed MCP server, Cortex REST APIs, official drivers, a Terraform provider and Python APIs. Snowflake says customer data is not used to train models; GA models get 60 days' deprecation notice, and drivers below 2026-10-27 minimum versions may be blocked.

Snowflake agent identity distinguishes delegated agents acting for a user from autonomous agents with their own SERVICE_AGENT identity. Cortex Agents, CoCo clients, CoWork and Snowflake-managed MCP sessions are marked agentic automatically, and custom OAuth integrations can set IS_AGENTIC = TRUE. Data policies can check IS_AGENT_ACTIVATED to hide data from agents, and activity is audited in QUERY_HISTORY.agent_type and ACCESS_HISTORY.agents_info. Release status is unconfirmed.

The Snowflake AI Credit is the single billing unit for Snowflake AI features, including Cortex Code, Cortex Agents, CoWork, Cortex REST API, AI Gateway, AI Functions and Cortex Search, priced the same across editions and regions. As of 2026-11-14 it costs $2.00 with global cross-region routing and $2.20 with regional routing. Capacity discounts do not apply but ACV-based AI Credit discounts do; the start date is unconfirmed.

A Snowflake authentication policy controls allowed authentication methods, client types, security integrations, MFA, PAT policy and workload identity policy; a user-level policy overrides the account one and by default everything is allowed. Creating one needs CREATE AUTHENTICATION POLICY on a schema, and applying it needs SECURITYADMIN or APPLY AUTHENTICATION POLICY. CLIENT_TYPES is best-effort and does not restrict REST API access.

Snowflake AWS PrivateLink provides private connectivity to Snowflake and requires Business Critical edition or higher. ACCOUNTADMIN authorizes it with SYSTEM$AUTHORIZE_PRIVATELINK and reads endpoint details from SYSTEM$GET_PRIVATELINK_CONFIG; URLs use a privatelink.snowflakecomputing.com form. After testing, block public access with a network policy; Azure and Google Cloud equivalents are documented separately.

Snowflake CLI (snow) is Snowflake's command-line tool, replacing SnowSQL; the latest release is 3.33.0 (2026-11-09), installed on Windows via PowerShell script, MSI or pip/pipx/uv. Connections live in connections.toml (shared with the CoCo CLI) and support password with MFA, key pair, OAuth, PAT, external browser and workload identity authenticators. Command groups include cortex and sql, and preview snow ai claude and snow ai opencode route local coding agents through Cortex AI Gateway.

Snowflake CoCo is Snowflake's AI coding agent, renamed from Cortex Code at Summit 2026 (2026-06-02), offered through Snowsight, a CLI, an Agent SDK, MCP, ACP and plugins. Cortex AI Guardrails have been GA for it since 2026-04-20. Docs still mix the CoCo and Cortex Code names, and the CLI binary is still called cortex.

The Snowflake CoCo (Cortex Code) CLI is an agentic coding CLI that orchestrates Snowflake skills and configured MCP tools and supports the Agent Client Protocol. It reuses the Snowflake CLI connections.toml file and requires the SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX_USER or SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX_AGENT_USER database role. It is not available on standard trial accounts; on Windows a PowerShell script installs the cortex executable, working natively or via WSL.

Snowflake Cortex AI is Snowflake's AI suite, covering Cortex Agents, AI Functions, Cortex Analyst, Fine-tuning, Search, CoWork, Cortex Code, AI Guardrails, AI Gateway and more. Its catalog includes GA Anthropic models up to claude-opus-5-5 and claude-sonnet-5-5 and OpenAI GPT-6 and GPT-5.x models, with others in preview. Most models are cross-region only, so access depends on cross-region inference; SHOW CORTEX BASE MODELS lists what a role can use.

Snowflake Cortex cross-region inference lets Cortex requests run outside the account's home region, controlled by the CORTEX_ENABLED_CROSS_REGION parameter, which only ACCOUNTADMIN can set. Values range from ANY_REGION and cloud-global scopes to geographies like AWS_US or DISABLED; new commercial organizations after 2026-03-09 default to ANY_REGION. Most Cortex models need it. Stored data stays home, prompts are not persisted, credits bill in the requesting region, and it is unavailable in China.

SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX_AGENT_USER is a Snowflake database role that is sufficient to call Cortex Agents and use the CoCo CLI, and is narrower than CORTEX_USER. It excludes Cortex Analyst, so agents with Analyst tools also need SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX_ANALYST_USER. A least-privilege agent runtime role holds it while CORTEX_USER is revoked from PUBLIC.

SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX_USER is the broad Snowflake database role covering all Covered AI Features, including Cortex Agents, AI Functions, Cortex Search, Cortex Analyst, CoWork, the Cortex REST API and the CoCo CLI. It is granted to PUBLIC by default; revoking it from PUBLIC is an AI opt-out control but does not block ACCOUNTADMIN. Narrower alternatives include CORTEX_AGENT_USER, CORTEX_ANALYST_USER, CORTEX_REST_API_USER and AI_FUNCTIONS_USER.

Snowflake CoWork, renamed from Snowflake Intelligence at Summit 2026 (2026-06-02), is Snowflake's conversational agent app at ai.snowflake.com where business users query data through Cortex Agents. Agents appear only when added to the CoWork object, and users need USAGE on agents and tool grants plus default role and warehouse; CORTEX_USER grants access. SQL keywords still say SNOWFLAKE INTELLIGENCE, uploads are limited to 5 files under 50 MB, and Guardrails have been GA since 2026-05-14.

The Snowflake CoWork object, SNOWFLAKE_INTELLIGENCE_OBJECT_DEFAULT (one per account, auto-created on the first settings change), controls which agents CoWork shows. Agents are added with ALTER SNOWFLAKE INTELLIGENCE ... ADD AGENT and users get USAGE on the object; creating it is held by ACCOUNTADMIN by default. It replaces the older method of creating agents in the SNOWFLAKE_INTELLIGENCE.AGENTS schema, with a documented migration path.

Snowflake External OAuth (TYPE = EXTERNAL_OAUTH) lets tokens from Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, PingFederate or custom authorization servers authenticate to Snowflake, and is the documented path for client-credentials machine-to-machine flows. Roles map from session:role scopes and users from a token claim. It has been GA for the managed MCP server since 2026-07-22. Privileged roles like ACCOUNTADMIN and SECURITYADMIN are blocked by default.

Snowflake key pair authentication uses an RSA key of at least 2048 bits for SERVICE and SERVICE_AGENT users, the CLI (SNOWFLAKE_JWT), the SQL API and REST APIs including Cortex Agents. REST calls send a KEYPAIR_JWT bearer token valid at most 1 hour. Two public key slots allow rotation, but named key pairs (ALTER USER ... ADD KEY PAIR) are now recommended because the legacy key supports neither role restriction nor expiration.

The Snowflake Labs MCP server (snowflake-labs-mcp, GitHub Snowflake-Labs/mcp) is an open-source, now deprecated and unmaintained MCP server, reportedly since 2026-05-15 with last release v1.4.2 (secondary). It points users to the Snowflake-managed MCP server. It ran via uvx with a YAML service config and authenticated through the Python connector; treat it as a legacy reference only.

The Snowflake Native App Framework packages apps as an application package (manifest, setup script, versions and patches) distributed through Marketplace or private listings. Apps can include Snowpark Container Services containers and Streamlit. Cortex Agents and MCP servers inside Native Apps have been GA since 2026-08-07, letting vendors ship agents into customer accounts.

A Snowflake network policy controls inbound access by combining network rules (IPv4, IPv6, AWS VPC endpoint IDs, Azure link IDs, compute pools) into allowed and blocked lists; block wins and integration policies override user and account ones. SECURITYADMIN or CREATE NETWORK POLICY is needed. SERVICE users must have one to use PATs, and it is used to block public access after PrivateLink is set up.

Snowflake OAuth (TYPE = OAUTH) is Snowflake's built-in authorization server using the authorization code flow with browser consent, for partner clients or custom clients; documented grants are only authorization_code and refresh_token, with access tokens of about 10 minutes. It is the default for the Snowflake-managed MCP server, using the user's default role, and works with REST, SQL API and CLI. Privileged roles are blocked by default, and a built-in local application integration was added 2026-01-21.

Snowflake OAuth token exchange issues per-task delegated tokens for agents per RFC 8693, via a POST to the account oauth/token endpoint with a subject token (OAuth, PAT or WIF), optional role scope, a Restricted Session Scope and an act claim. Exchanged tokens last one hour, have no refresh token and cannot be re-exchanged. Snowflake does not authenticate the caller or verify act, so keep subject tokens in the trusted tier. Release status is unconfirmed.

A Snowflake organization is a first-class object linking all accounts of one business entity for account management, billing, replication and failover, and data sharing. Snowflake creates it when the first account is provisioned, after which accounts can be added self-service. It can contain an organization account (for org admins and ORGANIZATION_USAGE views), regular and trial accounts, and Open Catalog accounts.

Snowflake per-user quotas cap AI spend per user and can block requests within minutes of the limit, across domains AI FUNCTION, SNOWFLAKE INTELLIGENCE, CORTEX AGENT, CORTEX CODE, AI GATEWAY and WAREHOUSE (blocking applies to AI domains only). Creating one needs SNOWFLAKE.QUOTA_CREATOR and CREATE SNOWFLAKE.CORE.QUOTA. They act faster than budgets, which take up to 8 hours. GA status is unconfirmed.

Snowflake programmatic access tokens (PATs) are bearer tokens for PERSON, SERVICE and SERVICE_AGENT users that authenticate REST APIs, SQL API, SCIM, SPCS, the managed MCP server and drivers. Default lifetime is 15 days (max 365) with up to 15 per user; the secret is shown once. SERVICE users need a network policy and ROLE_RESTRICTION, and Snowflake prefers OAuth for MCP. A PAT alone does not make a session agentic.

The Snowflake Python APIs (snowflake.core, installed with pip install snowflake) are GA and manage Snowflake resources declaratively from Python without SQL, including databases, warehouses, tasks, Snowpark Container Services and Cortex services. They support Python 3.10 to 3.14.

The Snowflake REST API is the HTTP interface through which Cortex Agents and other Snowflake resources are called. It accepts PATs, key-pair JWTs and OAuth tokens. For Cortex Agents, the X-Snowflake-Role header sets the role, otherwise the user's default role applies.

The Snowflake REST APIs are GA, OpenAPI-compliant resource APIs at the account URL under api/v2, covering users, roles, grants, warehouses, databases, tables, tasks, SPCS, network policies, integrations and Cortex Embed, Inference and Search. They accept bearer tokens typed as KEYPAIR_JWT (max 1 hour), OAUTH, PROGRAMMATIC_ACCESS_TOKEN or WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_FEDERATION. CREATE OR ALTER semantics support infrastructure-as-code, and specs are in the snowflake-rest-api-specs repo.

Snowflake SCIM provisioning syncs users and roles from Okta (OKTA_PROVISIONER), Microsoft Entra ID (AAD_PROVISIONER) or custom IdPs (GENERIC_SCIM_PROVISIONER) through a SCIM security integration. The provisioner role must own the users and roles it manages and needs CREATE USER and CREATE ROLE. SCIM token lifetime and generation details are unconfirmed.

The Snowflake Service Consumption Table is Snowflake's official rate card PDF for credits per million tokens, per message and per GB-month, including Cortex Agents billing units. Its PDF could not be parsed, so per-model AI Credit rates are not captured; a secondary source dates it 2026-09-30, but the effective date is unconfirmed.

A Snowflake SERVICE user (TYPE = SERVICE) is the non-human user type for programmatic integrations. It cannot use passwords or MFA, cannot have name or password attributes, and is not subject to authentication-policy MFA enforcement. It authenticates with key pair, OAuth, workload identity federation or PATs. Existing LEGACY_SERVICE users are migrated to SERVICE in Phase 3 (Aug to Oct 2026).

A Snowflake SERVICE_AGENT user (TYPE = SERVICE_AGENT) is the identity for an autonomous AI agent acting as itself; every session is agent-activated, and it can be managed via SQL or SCIM. It cannot use passwords or SAML SSO and authenticates with workload identity federation, key pair or PATs. The least-privilege pattern pairs it with a custom role holding CORTEX_AGENT_USER and only needed grants. Release status is unconfirmed.

The Snowflake SQL API is a REST endpoint at api/v2/statements for submitting SQL, checking status, fetching partitioned results and cancelling statements. It accepts OAuth, key pair and programmatic access tokens. It does not support PUT or GET, and transaction, USE, ALTER SESSION, session variables and temp objects work only in multi-statement requests.

Standard is the entry Snowflake edition; editions are Standard, Enterprise, Business Critical and Virtual Private Snowflake, each a superset of the previous. The editions page lists Cortex AI Functions, Cortex Analyst, Cortex Fine-tuning and Cortex Search for all editions, so Standard suffices for these AI features.

The Snowflake Terraform provider (snowflakedb/snowflake) manages Snowflake resources as code, typically authenticating with SNOWFLAKE_JWT key pair auth. The latest version is v2.23.0 (2026-11-05) and it requires Terraform 1.1.5 or later. Only v2.0.0+ stable resources are officially supported, preview resources need preview_features_enabled, and OpenTofu is not supported.

Snowflake workload identity federation gives SERVICE and SERVICE_AGENT users keyless authentication from AWS IAM roles, Azure managed identities or Entra ID, Google Cloud service accounts and OIDC issuers such as EKS, AKS, GKE, GitHub Actions, GitLab and SPIFFE. It is configured with CREATE USER ... WORKLOAD_IDENTITY and used via the WORKLOAD_IDENTITY authenticator in drivers and the CLI or a WIF bearer token on REST APIs. Configuring it on another user needs OWNERSHIP or MODIFY PROGRAMMATIC AUTHENTICATION METHODS.

The Snowflake-managed MCP server is a remote MCP server object created in an account, GA since 2025-11-04, exposing Cortex Agents, coding agent, Cortex Search, Analyst, SQL and UDF tools (max 50, responses truncated at 250 KB). It implements MCP 2025-11-25 tools only, responds to tool calls with SSE, and lacks dynamic client registration. It defaults to Snowflake OAuth, supports External OAuth (GA 2026-07-22) and PATs; server USAGE does not grant tool access. It is not FedRAMP-assessed or replicated.

Snowpark Container Services (SPCS) is Snowflake's container runtime, built from image repositories, compute pools, long-running services and job services, available in AWS, Azure and GCP commercial regions with exceptions. Outbound network access needs an external access integration. It hosts Native App containers and the Openflow deployment, and uses Snowflake-created SNOWFLAKE_SERVICE users. GPU families and quantitative limits are unconfirmed.

SnowSQL is Snowflake's legacy command-line client, replaced by Snowflake CLI, which alone gets new features. SnowSQL 1.5.x is supported through 2028-04-16. Migration uses snow helpers import-snowsql-connections, with flag changes such as --config-file, --format json, --stdin for piped input and -D variables.

The SQLcl MCP server is Oracle's local stdio MCP server, started with sql -mcp, that uses SQLcl saved connections and offers tools such as connect, run-sql, run-sqlcl and schema-information. Restrict levels are set with -R; the 25.4 docs say the default is the most restrictive level 4, but a later changelog says it now defaults to unrestricted, which is newer but unconfirmed by version. Every request is logged to the DBTOOLS$MCP_LOG table.

Standard PayGo is Google's per-token standard consumption model for Gemini on Agent Platform, replacing dynamic shared quota. Usage runs on shared capacity with an organization-level tier set by 30-day spend; Tier 4 (above $50,000) was added 2026-09-10. Tier TPM thresholds are prioritization levels, not hard caps (for example Pro models 500K to 10M, Flash models 2M to 50M). A 429 means temporary contention, fixed by backoff, smoothing spikes and the global endpoint.

The Terraform Google provider (hashicorp/google, latest 8.11.0 from 2026-11-10, with companion google-beta) manages Google Cloud resources as code. Agent Runtime is managed with google_vertex_ai_reasoning_engine resources, Agent Gateway needs google-beta, and Gemini Enterprise apps and data stores use discovery_engine resources. No resource for Gemini Enterprise agent registration was found.

The Terraform OCI provider (oracle/oci) manages Oracle Cloud Infrastructure resources as code; the latest version is v9.13.0 (2026-11-11). It can authenticate as an instance principal and has Generative AI Agents resources such as oci_generative_ai_agent_agent. Recent additions include model discovery and routing profiles, GenAI API key support and bring-your-own reservations for dedicated AI clusters.

Unity Catalog is Databricks' governance layer, with a metastore > catalog > schema > objects hierarchy covering tables, volumes, functions, models and secrets, plus connections and credentials outside the schema tree. It is often enabled by default on newer accounts, and the metastore admin manages privileges. Agent-relevant privileges include READ VOLUME, USE CONNECTION, ACCESS and CREATE SERVICE. Unity Gateway builds on it to govern models, agents, MCP servers and tools as securables.

A Unity Catalog HTTP connection is a Databricks securable that stores credentials for calling an external HTTP service, and backs external MCP servers registered as Unity Gateway MCP services. Auth types include bearer token, OAuth M2M (recommended), OAuth U2M shared or per-user, dynamic client registration and Databricks-managed OAuth providers. Schema-level connections are GA and metastore-level ones Public Preview.
